subject: Is it possible to run each pair of configuration+Instance number of time?

messages.author: 01dd2037cabee038
messages.subject: Is it possible to run each pair of configuration+Instance number of time?
parts:
Hi,

I have an nondeterministic algorithm, so in order to raise the creditability of the result for each pair of configuration+Instance, I would want to run each pair number of time and than to take the median/average result as the cost of this pair.
I am not sure if this is possible. The only related option I found is the "deterministic" option, but it not allowed me to control the amount of runs for each configuration+Instance.

Thank you & Best regard,
Naama

messages.author: 854a0709976c2a48
messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to run each pair of configuration+Instance number of time?
parts:
Hi Naama,

If irace runs out of instances, it will start replicating instances with different seeds (unless the algorithm is deterministic). You don't have to do anything (except use the seed that irace generates to make sure your runs are indeed different).

If you still would prefer to have a fixed number of runs per instance instead of letting irace control this (because you have some knowledge that the variance within instances is much larger than the variance between instances), then you can do several runs per instance in your target-runner and report to irace only the mean/median. However, I would suggest to compare such a setup with simply letting irace choose how many runs per instance to do on its own (but adjusting--first-test and  --each-test to 5*nruns and nruns, respectively, where nruns is the number of runs you want to do per instance). My intuition is that the latter setup will produce better results. I'll be interested in knowing if this is not the case.

In any case, if you can have obtain or generate more training instances, it is always better to do add more training instances and do one run per instance rather than fewer instances and more runs. See

M. Birattari. On the estimation of the expected performance of a metaheuristic on a class of
instances. how many instances, how many runs? Technical Report TR/IRIDIA/2004-001,
IRIDIA, Université Libre de Bruxelles, Belgium, 2004.

for the detailed explanation.

Cheers,

Manuel.
